title: BioDynaSpec: Harmonic-Guided Spatio-Spectral Autoregressive Diffusion for Protein Dynamics Generation
claim: Decomposing signals into windowed frequency bands, then generating low-to-high frequency with a structure-aware bias, separates global motion from local fluctuation.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, transform then generation then structural bias
description: Three panels read left to right. The left panel, 'Time → Frequency Domain', shows a time axis cut into four windows with overlapping gray trajectory curves. Gray arrows labeled 'Independent FFT' lead down to orange high-frequency local fluctuations and a blue low-frequency global motion curve, with a frequency axis alongside. The middle panel, 'Frequency-wise Generation', is a grid of residue rows by frequency columns F1–F5. Cell color runs from blue (low frequency) to orange (high frequency), and a large gray arrow marks autoregression over frequency from low to high. The right panel, 'Inter-Residue Harmonic Bias', shows a 3D protein backbone with red and orange highlights for strong connections (peptide and hydrogen bonds) and yellow for faint ones (van der Waals). An inset shows a Gaussian distance-bias curve, exp(−τ·d²).
caption: Motivation of BioDynaSpec. (Left) IWFD transforms windowed trajectories into the frequency domain to disentangle global
abstract: Generating long-horizon molecular dynamics (MD) is difficult due to error accumulation in time-domain autoregressive models, which causes drift, and fixed step-size constraints on temporal resolution. We propose **BioDynaSpec**, which reformulates protein dynamics as spatio-spectral generation: **Independent Windowed Fourier Decomposition (IWFD)** decomposes trajectories into window-wise spectral representations, and a generator combines low-to-high frequency autoregression with diffusion denoising to reconstruct continuous motion. This formulation is motivated by **a local near-equilibrium view of protein dynamics**: after per-window alignment, fluctuations around an anchor conformation are better characterized in spectral space, where local mode structure is more explicit than in frame-wise coordinates. To improve cross-residue and cross-frequency consistency, we introduce **Inter-Residue Frequency Coupling (IRFC)**, a learnable Gaussian distance bias in attention that injects a resonance-inspired structural prior. On ATLAS, BioDynaSpec improves 250-frame trajectory generation with $R_{250}=1.509$ Å, where $R_s$ denotes the mean per-frame C$\alpha$-RMSE over the first $s$ frames after alignment, reducing error by 60.4\% versus MDGEN and 57.2\% versus ProAR, while achieving the best PCA-2D displacement-profile correlation and stepwise distribution matching. For equilibrium conformational sampling, it achieves Root Mean $W_2=1.31$, MD PCA $W_2=0.90$, and Joint PCA $W_2=1.19$, improving over the next best method by 50.03\%, 35.25\%, and 47.58\%, respectively. It also improves near-equilibrium local-dynamics and covariance consistency, achieving PCA-PSD-LogCorr $=0.817$ and CFRE $=0.989$, corresponding to a 21.9\% gain and a 36.7\% reduction over the next best method, respectively. The source code is available at https://github.com/Linmj-Judy/BioDynaSpec.git.
